turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll explore the repo structure first to locate streaming-related implementation files.I have enough to answer comprehensively now. Let me also check `EventStream.ts` briefly and `ChatCompletionStream.ts` static entry point to confirm the pattern, and check `client.ts`/`api-promise.ts` for how the raw request flows into `defaultParseResponse`.This confirms the full chain: `client.post()`/`.get()` builds an `APIPromise` whose `parseResponse` is `defaultParseResponse` (src/internal/parse.ts), which checks `options.stream` and delegates to `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (or a resource-specific `__streamClass`).

## Where streaming is implemented

**Low-level SSE/stream engine** — `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `export class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` — the core primitive. Parses Server-Sent Events into an async iterator.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — turns a raw `fetch` `Response` into a `Stream`, using the internal `_iterSSEMessages()` generator, `SSEDecoder`, and `LineDecoder` (from `src/internal/decoders/line`) to split the byte stream on SSE frames (`data:`/`event:` lines, double-newline boundaries) and `JSON.parse` each payload.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — alternate constructor for newline-delimited JSON streams (non-SSE).
- Also provides `tee()` (split for independent consumption) and `toReadableStream()`.
- `src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export shim (`export * from './core/streaming'`).

**Wiring into responses** — `src/internal/parse.ts`
- `defaultParseResponse()` is the function every `APIPromise` uses to turn a raw HTTP response into a typed value (`src/core/api-promise.ts:24-27`, default `parseResponse`).
- If `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` if a resource specifies a custom stream class, otherwise falls back to the base `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)`.

**Higher-level "helper" streaming runners** (build on `Stream`, add typed events/accumulation):
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — generic `EventStream<EventTypes>` base class (event emitter + abort/end/done lifecycle) used by the two runners below.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `class ResponseStream<ParsedT> extends EventStream<ResponseEvents>`. Wraps `client.responses.create({ ...params, stream: true })` or `client.responses.retrieve(id, { stream: true })`, consumes the low-level `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>`, accumulates snapshots (`accumulateResponse`), and re-emits typed events (`response.output_text.delta`, etc.) plus a `finalResponse()` promise.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` (and `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`, `src/lib/AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts`) — analogous wrapper for Chat Completions, extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `class AssistantStream extends EventStream<AssistantStreamEvents>`, used by the (deprecated) Assistants API.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({ stream: true })` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:98-123` | `this._client.post('/responses', { stream: body.stream ?? false })` → `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, { stream: true })` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:142-169` | same pattern via `this._client.get(...)` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:201-206` | `ResponseStream.createResponse()` — helper wrapper |
| `client.chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | `this._client.post('/chat/completions', { stream: body.stream ?? false })` → `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:221-226` | `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(params)` (when `stream: true`) | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:195-212` | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools()` |
| `client.completions.create({ stream: true })` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-44` | same `stream:` post pattern → `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, { stream: true })` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-83` | `this._client.post(...)` with `__synthesizeEventData: true` → `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` (deprecated) | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:165-234` | `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()` |
| `client.audio.speech.create(...)` | `src/resources/audio/speech.ts:29-35` | Different mechanism: `__binaryResponse: true` returns the raw `Response` object directly (audio byte stream), not the SSE `Stream` class |
| `bedrock` provider `.responses.stream` | `src/bedrock.ts` (per search hit) | wraps the same `API.Responses['stream']` |

Every non-binary streaming call ultimately bottoms out at `props.options.stream` being read in `src/internal/parse.ts`, which hands off to `Stream.fromSSEResponse` in `src/core/streaming.ts`.

## What I did not verify
- `src/resources/completions.ts` (legacy) content beyond the `create` overloads shown — didn't confirm it has no `.stream()` helper (evidence suggests it doesn't, only `chat.completions` and `responses` do).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` internals (event accumulation logic) — only confirmed its class declaration and that `completions.ts` imports/calls it; didn't read the full accumulator logic (parallel to `ResponseStream`'s `accumulateResponse`).
- `src/bedrock.ts` and `src/resources/realtime/*` streaming (WebSocket-based, e.g. `ws-base.ts` seen in search) — these use a different (WebSocket) transport, not the SSE `Stream` class; I did not read `ws-base.ts` in full.
- Whether other resources (e.g. `videos`, `containers`) expose `stream: true` params — not checked beyond the grep/search results shown above.

# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/

import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
